notes: ACCESS: Claude-in-Chrome only, own tab. robots.txt is 48 chars ('User-agent: *' + one Disallow line), names no Claude/anthropic agent - no block. Loaded https://fermliving.com/?country=DK once to pin the Shopify Markets context (Shopify.country=='DK', cookie localization=DK confirmed in page) exactly as the prior Home-Decor pass did; without it this session's geo-IP market deflates catalogue results. No 403/WAF/CAPTCHA/rate-limit at any point. TREE: taken as the union of (a) the mega-menu, read out of the DOM - the header carries 11 data-dynamic-menu-parent top-level nodes (Kids, Outdoor Living, Accessories, Furniture, Sofas, Lighting, Kitchen, Textiles, Rugs, Certified Products, Spare Parts) with their child columns, (b) the site's own full collection universe via same-origin /collections.json?limit=250 (186 collections, all handles+titles+products_count scanned locally against a furniture keyword list), and (c) each category page's own server-rendered sub-category chip strip (fetched same-origin for furniture, sofas-and-daybeds, outdoor-furniture, kids, storage, shelves). All three agreed exactly - no furniture node exists outside the mega-menu on this store, so §7b trap 1 produced nothing extra here. QTY METHOD: this Shopify theme renders NO product-count header anywhere on a collection page (verified on /collections/tables: zero '\d+ (products|items|results)' matches in body innerText), so Rule 1 is unobtainable and Rule 3 full enumeration was used - same-origin fetch of /collections/<handle>/products.json?limit=250 paged until an empty page, de-duplicated on the numeric Shopify product id, under the DK market session. As an independent cross-check every one of the 19 handles enumerated returned a unique-id count IDENTICAL to that collection's products_count in /collections.json (tables 143, chairs 105, stools 14, lounge-chairs-and-poufs 112, poufs 75, daybeds 26, storage 108, shelves 69, outdoor-furniture 97, outdoor-seating 65, outdoor-tables 31, 2/3/4-seaters 30/28/11, kids-furniture 105, kids-storage 50, furniture 677, sofas-and-daybeds 295, small-storage 150). That reproduces the prior pass's finding that products_count is NOT inflated on this particular store; the qty recorded is the enumeration, with products_count agreeing. SANITY CHECKS: numbers differ per node (no site-wide constant); no round display caps; every leaf URL fetched to HTTP 200 with an h1/canonical matching the requested slug; a deliberately bogus slug (/collections/w148-bogus-slug-test) returns a real HTTP 404 to the /404 canonical, so this platform does NOT silently serve a parent listing for a bad slug (§7b trap 2 disproved here). Node identity taken from the slug, not the label (§7b trap 3) - note /collections/lounge-chairs-and-poufs carries the display title 'Lounge Chairs' and shares ZERO product ids with /collections/poufs (set-intersection check), so they are genuinely disjoint sibling leaves despite the handle. HIERARCHY / §2: 'Furniture' (677) is a pure grouping row - set arithmetic shows its 9 nav children cover exactly 677/677 unique ids, so it is never recorded as a leaf. 'Outdoor Furniture' (97) is likewise a grouping row: outdoor-seating (65) and outdoor-tables (31) are strict subsets of it (65/65 and 31/31 ids inside) covering 96 of 97, so the two deeper nodes are recorded instead (1 product in outdoor-furniture sits in neither child). 'Sofas' (/collections/sofas-and-daybeds, 295) is a grouping row with the three size children 2-Seater/3-Seater/4-Seater Sofas (30/28/11 = 69 ids). Its remaining ~226 products are modular-sofa modules that the site exposes only through named design-line collections - Catena Modular Sofas (135), Dase Modular Sofas (48), Rico Sofas and Divans (76), Rico Modular Sofas (21), Turn (14) - each of which also has a /pages/<name> marketing landing page; these are product/design collections and are excluded under §3, which is why the three size leaves do not sum to the parent. EXCLUDED: /collections/furniture, /collections/sofas-and-daybeds and /collections/outdoor-furniture as view-all parents (§2); fabric-samples (61) as furniture parts/samples; /pages/punctual-shelving-system and its collection punctual-shelving-system (35) as a single named product line (§3); sale-furniture (40) as a Sale node (§3); the room landing collections the-living-room / the-bedroom / the-dining-room-see-what-is-coming / the-office / the-hallway and all '-see-what-is-coming' and 'at-home-with-*' pages as mixed editorial/room pages, not categories; all Lighting, Mirrors, Kitchen, Textiles, Rugs, Accessories, Wallpaper, Wall Decorations branches per §1. KIDS: kids-furniture (105) IS kept - a local title scan shows kids desks, tables, chairs, stools, benches, bookcases, a junior bed, a high chair, a dresser, a cupboard and poufs/bean bags, i.e. primary product type is furniture. kids-storage (50) is DROPPED - title scan: TOTAL 50 / clear standalone storage goods 22+ by keyword (braided storage baskets, wall pockets, paper-pulp boxes, canvas pockets, storage bags, woven baskets) against only ~7 furniture items (Slope Bookcase, Giraffe/Horse Bookcase, Slope Storage Bench, Sill Cupboard, Tukki Trolley, Isola Storage Table); the site files it under the Kids menu, not under a Furniture department, so it reads as the Storage task's scope, not this one. STOCK NOTE (§7b trap 4): products.json returns published products regardless of stock, so these are catalogue counts, not in-stock snapshots; no node read 0 or absurdly low.
